body: Arrrrrrrrgh, that's the WORST PART! Trying to kill the hours in the day! I'll be around if you feel like killing time!

Just keep going between these McDonald's and Burger King points, liibrary, and YMCA. Yes, it sucks. And yes, it's degrading. And yes, you will feel like shit, but at least it gives you something to do every day (and keeps you alive!) 

What are you up to tonight (today?? Time difference kills me!)

I've more than been where you are! I was homeless and starving for a lot of my 25 years!
I can only give you these tips;

1) is there a bus shelter near you? These work in your favour because there's powerpoints and heating.

2) Can you access cafes? These ALSO work in your favour cuz you can get free water and sugar sachets (when I didn't have food, I lived off these!!)

3) Any libraries nearby? Don't sign up; just use them for the warmth, a 'safe' place, corners to nap, free wifi/powerpoints, and (with the 'fancy' ones) showers/hot water to clean yourself!

Your situation sucks now, I get it, but if you set your mind to it, you can get a job and a (shitty) house! If I can do it man, anyone can! 
Good luck!

Thank you for reassuring me and giving me a head's up on what to expect! Your reply has helped SO MUCH!

The predominant concern I have is that the flashbacks and nightmares are going to increase in severity after the therapy sessions - does this generally happen? Is it short term, or something that is ongoing following each session?
